title: MZ Welcome to Elderfield [Spooky Farming RPG // Alpha Demo]

posts.author: chris-cote
posts.body:
Welcome to Elderfield is a spooky farming RPG
​
You can farm, fish, mine, cook, craft, befriend townsfolk, beseech the old gods, investigate mysteries, watch unsettling news programs, get lost in the dead mall, die in your sleep and more. There's lots to do in Elderfield.
The game is currently in its alpha demo stage, but has had extensive bug fixes, balancing updates, feature additions and more. There is currently 10-20 hours of gameplay (though some have logged much more!).
If this sounds like a game you might like, please consider giving it a try and, if you enjoy it, leaving a Steam review.
I am looking for all bug reports, feedback, and suggestions. I want the game to be bug-free, but also fun, balanced and polished.

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Heyas, I gave your demo a try but had to stop because it was just running way too slow... Which is a real shame since I wanted to play this game.
Spoiler:
Feedback
I really couldn't play much of it, but the aesthetics of the game are great. From the Pop! horror tiles to the Junji Ito-inspired character art, it's clear you've put a lot of work into making it look just how you want it.
Unfortunately, I think that's where the problems start. I was barely hitting 40 FPS, which made even biking around the town feel like I was moving through molasses. While I don't have the greatest laptop, it still can normally run rpg maker games no problem unless there's either an issue with a plugin or parallel processes. There seems to be a lot of filter effects going on with the game, so I think that may be where part of your problem is coming from. It may be good to add some options to the game that let players turn all the filters off, so that the game can run better. Though if you do that and it's still slow, it could be due to something else. It's hard to even guess where the lag is coming from, so you may need to do a few tests with slower computers to see if you can pinpoint what can fix it.
I went to the farm... And it got stuck loading. I gave it a few minutes, but it just didn't seem to want to load so I had to call it quits. I wanted to play this since I love farming sims, but apparently the eldritch gods involved in this game said no. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
There were a few other bugs and oddities:
The game has a zipped project file of itself inside the zip, adding to the file size
Can't configure the controls in the Options menu, even though it's listed
While I can understand why the radio is audio-only, for your hard of hearing players it would be good to include a transcript
Why can't you prepare a meal using the Cooking Pot with stuff still in the fridge? It would be nice if it could pull from there
Minor thing, but it would be nice if the deposit/withdraw window started at 1 automatically instead of starting at 0
For the battle tutorial, it may be better to use the full screen for a message box instead of separating out each bit with normal-sized message boxes
Can't scroll up from the top of a list for some strange reason
The die effect when searching is interesting, but I'm only getting 1s. Is that cuz I'm looking through the trash? Also, shorten it a bit so it's snappier
Overall, I can't say whether this game is good or not. But I can say that it really needs optimized so that it runs at a decent speed. I hope you can get it fixed, since I do want to play this at some point, so I'll be keeping an eye on the thread.
Good luck with your project!

I've made some changes in the last few updates which should hopefully fix a few of your problems.
The controls settings have been reworked, so they may work for you now. Please let me know if they do, as I have another avenue to explore if they still don't.
I have added a few performance options to the main menu, namely disabling weather effects, fog effects and footstep sounds. These should all improve performance. I plan to add more toggles soon for screen filters and lighting effects, which should help further.
I am also working with the plugin developer to address some of your inventory/crafting-related feedback, such as starting deposit/withdraw quantities at 1, pulling cooking ingredients from the fridge directly, and adding some other features while we're at it (such as setting the withdraw/deposit quantity to max by pressing left from 0, and making the storage menu item icons consistent with the inventory). It seems that these changes should be possible within a week or so.
Also, the die-roll effect is now much faster.
The download in the OP is always a link to the latest version, so you can try the new changes there.

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Heyas, I'm back! I gave your v0.0.19 demo a try and was able to actually visit the farm! However, I think this game just doesn't want me to play and enjoy my time, I have apparently been cursed by the eldritch gods of this game.
Spoiler:
Feedback
Let me start with a few of the things you've tweaked.
The game does run better now, and turning off some of the effects did seem to help. It still ran slow for me, but there were points where I sped around at what I assume is the correct speed so it wasn't terrible to explore now. The controls in the Options menu now works, and I could make changes so that was nice. The die roll definitely felt better, which was nice since I got to see if a lot more often this time.
But now that I could actually play, I did end up finding out a horrible truth: this game uses a lot of RNG. And if there is one consistent thing when it comes to me playing a game, it is that I have terrible, horrible, no good, very bad luck! Out of all my die rolls, I saw a five or six twice and more than half of them were ones. Which meant that a lot of the time I was getting cursed or injured when trying to interact with mysteries, and didn't get an item most of the time when searching trash cans. The game's RNG decided that I was not allowed to enjoy the game. Sleeping? Cursed. Staying up all night? Cursed. Battles? Miss an attack and get killed. Fishing?
Killed
The QTE point appeared at the far side of the bar so I had no chance to hit it in time.
It's extra work for you as a dev, but it may be good to add in a 'this person has bad luck' modifier. Even if an event has a 50-50 chance to be good, players will mostly focus on the failures, so being able to tweak their luck behind the scenes could help players feel like the game isn't just trying to make them lose. Track their curses, and if they've been cursed two nights in a row? Give them a break and have a normal night. Has your player rolled 4 ones in a row? Throw them a bone and give them a three so they get a neutral luck reward. RNG can add a lot to a game and replayability, but it also can quickly make a player feel like the game is unfair so balancing things out a bit behind the scenes can help.
The farming itself worked well, and I would have spent more time just watering crops and sleeping so they'd grow but I had crows keep eating some of them (I did set up a scarecrow and it helped a bit, but I still lost 3 of 8 wheats) and I rarely had money so I could afford to buy more seeds unless I sold off all the food I had made.
Battles were punishing, to the point that I gave up on going to the mall at all. I tried to up my hit rate with equipment since I was missing often, but even when I did kill an enemy in 3 or 4 turns they would do tons of damage to me. And if I died, the enemies would all respawn so any progress I had made was wiped out. Most of the time the enemy bodies were too far gone for me to search for items (which I'm guessing is luck-based), and even if I did get some Mystery Meat from them I tended to use up more food to heal than I gained. I did consider just spending a bunch of days collecting herbs and mushrooms in the main town area to stock up on food, but that just didn't feel like a fun way to spend my afternoon so I gave up that plan.
I do want to emphasize that this game looks great and the writing is pretty entertaining! And the concept behind the mechanics is good, it's just that the RNG seemed to want me to only fail, and that lead to a harsh time while playing.
There were a few other bugs and oddities:
Skipping the tutorial makes the gate open right away, but doesn't give the player the Wooden Stick or a first fight. Either force the player to do that part, or auto-equip the Wooden Stick so they can fully skip that. Also, the rat is un-fightable since the event just repeats the "go equip the stick" message
Nice to include Performance Options! But the Footsteps Sounds on/off seems to be tied to the FPS on/off too
What if the die roll took place in the center of the screen, instead of at the bottom?
The farm loads now, but it still has quite a delay. May want to play around with interesting loading screens if it will happen often
The shopping screen doesn't have a limit you can hit if you have at least enough money for one item. So instead of being able to easily hit the max number I can afford, I need to actually adjust to reach the number
When trying to plant seeds, why not have the 'Select Seed' option appear first, instead of 'Plant Seed' since planting won't work without selecting? Also, what if there was an icon next to the 'Plant Seed' that showed which seed was currently equiped?
It seems like most of the important NPCs give a gift of equipment, may be good to include a little tag (like [Head] or [Body]) in those messages so people realize the gifts need to be equipped back at home
Death is meaningless when you have no money. While it may be cruel, if your player is broke maybe consider giving them a minor Curse instead of taking 0 gold. Or have Death feel bad for the unlucky players and give them a blessing to help them out
Having a Warp ability is very useful, but why hide it away in the video store?
The Help menu options starts at Husbandry, not at the start of the list
The fishing minigame is broken! If you try fishing in the lake, it sets the clock to 23:30(ish) of that day, so literal days will pass if you try to catch a few fish
Overall, this game has a lot of promise! But between my luck and the heavy use of RNG I just couldn't make a lot of progress. I hope your target players have better luck than I did.
Good luck with your project!

Thanks again for all of this feedback!
I'll go through it bit by bit, in order:
I'm glad it runs better now! I just released a new update a few mins ago which adds even more performance toggles (like lighting effects and day/night transitions, which should have significant improvements). I have another toggle planned for screen filters in the future as well, pending some more plugin work.
Regarding RNG - this is SUPER helpful feedback. While an element of randomness is intentional, I do want to avoid "feels bad" gameplay. I am not trying to make the next Fear & Hunger, as much as I do like that game, haha. I have made some significant changes to random elements of the game based on this feedback in the latest update, including:
A 30% higher chance of getting rewards from garbage (and a more accurate roll result to reflect your actual luck stat)
A decrease in how punishing bad results from mysteries are (their rewards overall trend very positive)
Some tweaks to how common the good results are (slightly more common)
Some good mystery rewards have been improved
A 50% lower chance for crows to eat your crops
Fishing is now slightly easier (larger bar starting length)
This is all just a start, but I am considering other changes to help further, such as adding more luck to the stats of early game equipment. My goal is for it to at least not be frustrating at all, even for someone that doesn't like RNG based games. The game's focus is more on farming, making money, and progressing than gambling.
I am open to adding "luck correction" mechanics to the game, but I am mainly just waiting on more feedback before I implement anything like that. As I make these simple tweaks and see how they affect gameplay for players, I can gauge whether more drastic measures are needed.
I'm glad you like the farming! As mentioned before, crows now eat far less crops, and I may reduce this even further, so hopefully that helps. I found the crows annoying even in my own testing, and already made the scarecrows easier to craft than they used to be.
A recent update increased the sell price of all crops, and it is something I am looking at regularly. The recent addition of animal raising and some food processing to higher value items has improved the profitability as well, and I am working on adding some other ways to process crops to earn more money, so that may help.
I may also increase the crop prices after all of that is done if it still isn't enough, or make more farming plots available earlier.
Battles are indeed pretty punishing in the beginning, though something to keep in mind is that there are not very many of them. This is something I am struggling a bit with in terms of communicating to the player that beating even one enemy is a big deal. I think in total there are about 12 pre-determined battle locations in the entire demo, and each one opens up some new content (characters, items, quests, mysteries, even entire mechanics), so the idea is to take a "slow and steady" pace. Since they are unlikely to respawn unless you die, the idea is to beat whatever enemies you have food for, and decide whether to rest and do something else, or avoid resting while you gather more resources to push further.
I am definitely having some trouble communicating the intended pacing of the game, and I think players are used to blowing through 2-3+ fights like its nothing at the start of a game. I am open to any suggestions there for telegraphing the pacing better (maybe not letting them into the mall too early? Or maybe some kind of warning, or a quest to misdirect them into doing something easier first while they prepare. idk).
Regarding your list of bugs etc.:
Good catch! I am re-doing this part of the tutorial, so that will all be sorted in an update soon.
This is now fixed, no more random FPS toggles!
The reason it is near the bottom is because it looked odd when it would cover up the player, or what you were interacting with. This way, it is where you would expect to see text instead.
A farm loading image (maybe even animation) is definitely in the plans! On a PC with a dedicated graphics card it should only take a couple of seconds to load, but on lower end devices I can definitely see that plain screen getting boring to look at.
The shopping item max is in the plans for a future update. The deposit/withdraw quantities now work this way (and start at 1 by default), so the shop is next on the list for these QoL changes.
"Select Seed" is second because once you have one selected, you can then mash A to keep planting, instead of pressing down past "Select Seed". I may change it so it changes the order depending on whether you have a seed selected, though I am also considering rethinking that menu a bit in general, but either way this will be addressed.
I am looking into having a new plugin developed to have some kind of on-screen notification when an item is added to the wardrobe, so that it is clear what the player just found.
More death penalties is a possibility, but I do have to be careful when the fights can already be challenging. Resetting enemies is a punishment in itself, so I want to keep the feels-bads to a minimum. The "hard" difficulty is also there for players who want a harsher death penalty.
Hiding the warp is to encourage some exploration, add a reward to beating the first mall enemy, and is early enough that you won't be travelling too far from home at that point anyways. That said, I may consider moving it earlier in the mall (before the fight).
The help menu order has been fixed in the new update
The fishing minigame is now fixed!
Also, regarding your previous feedback:
- More performance toggles are now in the game, with still more to come
- Default withdraw/deposit quantities are now 1
- Pressing left/down sets the withdraw/deposit amount to the max available, and loops
- Cooking now takes ingredients directly from the fridge. I will be adding special storage for crafting at the forge and the farm as well in the future.
Thanks again for all of this feedback! It is extremely useful.
